GTA 6’s Digital Release Has GameStop CEO Defending Physical Games, For Obvious Reasons

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • According to recent reports, the GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit.
  • Sources indicate that "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen stated to Bloomberg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The GTA 6 launch looks set to break several records, as the digital-only game appears on track to be a major critical and commercial hit. Right on cue, GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has criticized publishers that forgo a traditional physical release as a business strategy that hurts consumers and GameStop's bottom line, without explicitly mentioning GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive. "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it, or lend it to a friend," Cohen remarked to Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all-digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop. Of course they don't like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying fresh. They're taking away competition." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RQvBOySNq1U Cohen's comments come in the wake of GTA 6 being a digital-only release--the "physical" edition includes a download code for it. It's also somewhat ironic for Cohen to defend physical games, given the GameStop boss's July remarks that physical video games were "irrelevant" to GameStop's business strategy. That business model has relied heavily on secondhand game sales, and none of those profits ever made their way back to the original publishers. Right now, GameStop indicates that selling video game software makes up the smallest part of its business. But in the case of GTA 6? Going digital probably made financial sense for Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games. The entire game clocks in at over 211GB, which means three standard 100GB Ultra HD Blu-ray discs would have been needed to house GTA 6 in its launch-day entirety--although realistically, Take-Two probably would have opted for one disc and forced consumers to download the rest of the game. That would have raised costs, and it wouldn't be unlikely to imagine Take-Two fearing the discs being reverse-engineered for secrets ahead of GTA 6's launch. Going digital essentially removed those risks, and while PlayStation and Xbox do take a cut of profits for hosting the game on their servers. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 sales for PS5 alone have reached $1.38 billion in revenue so far, which means Sony is profiting handsomely from those sales. Retailers are still entitled to a share of the profits for stocking the code-in-a-box version of the game on their shelves, and once you start to factor in distribution costs, Take-Two's reasoning starts to make sense. The publisher says 98% of its business is digital, but it's not ruling out a proper physical GTA 6 edition in the future. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grimes is speaking out after publicly opposing her former partner Elon Musk’s well-documented interest in artificial intelligence.

“Super intelligence will hack your limbic system,” Musk, 55, wrote via his X platform on Tuesday, November 17, resharing an announcement about the first AI-generated influencer.

Grimes, 38, responded in the comments section, tweeting, “The fixation on fake women feels like cope. I’m a fan of Claudia, but she doesn’t have a birkin deal and she isn’t a she, she’s an alien creature who’s both blessed and haunted by the entirety of ancestral memory.“.

She continued, “Secualizing [sic] a species that cannot have sex is the ultimate definition of Nietzsche’s last man, and we can do better than reducing ‘it’ to a sex slave.” (For the uninitiated, philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche introduced the concept of “the last man” in 1883, offering a cautionary tale of lazy nihilism in which humans give up on creativity, creation, and the experience of struggle for comfort and and safety.).

Recent findings suggest that while Musk has not publicly addressed Grimes’ public criticism, the singer’s rep offered further insight into her decision to speak out in opposition to the father of her children. (Grimes and Musk share sons X Æ A-Xii, 6, and Techno Mechanicus, 4, as well as daughter Exa Dark Sideræl, 4. (Musk also shares 11 additional kids with three other women.).

“Grimes opposes unelected power, and that includes Mr. Musk’s unelected power,” Grimes’ spokesperson Mitchell Jackson told Us in a statement. “Given Mr. Musk’s power, Grimes believes it’s ridiculous that Mr. Musk behaves this way and spends his free time promoting AI slop while needlessly lowering morale and alienating the people.”.

Jackson added, “Grimes is disappointed in the lack of maturity and leadership from the tech giants. She will continue to speak out on this vital topic and welcomes the discourse surrounding these tweets. Grimes believes we cannot afford any more of this aggressive nihilism from those in power. She will continue to speak out about these important concerns.”.

Grimes is set to further address her tech safety concerns in her forthcoming record, including the newly released single “DeepSeek.”.

Recent findings suggest that “DeepSeek’ is about machine welfare,” Jackson noted in his statement. “It’s clear tech leaders do not care about AI safety for humans or machines.”.

Grimes and Musk were in a relationship from 2018 to 2022, since going back and forth about coparenting arrangements and social media guidelines for their three children.

It has been revealed that “I, unfortunately, do not control the internet and cannot wipe this from the internet. I have tried begging the public and my kids’ dad to keep them offline,” Grimes tweeted in March 2025, claiming she asked Musk not to show their kids’ faces publicly. “The state of my children’s lives being public is of grave concern to me and I think about how to solve this every day. It’s insane to me that there’s no way to deal with this.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's promptly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

It has been revealed that this earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her new direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

In a recent development, when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very quickly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she notes more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

According to recent reports, certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

She'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. This very dark comedy-drama follows a free-spirited, deeply angry single young woman living in London and sharing her romantic ups and downs via confessional asides to us, the audience. She falls, rather reluctantly, for "The Priest" (Andrew Scott)—while she's a confirmed atheist, and he's obviously not, the show doesn't turn aside from the general messiness of the situation. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, maisel was one of Prime’s first truly buzzy original series, a comedy-drama from Amy Sherman-Palladino (Gilmore Girls) about the title’s Midge Maisel (Rachel Brosnahan), a long-time Fresh York housewife of the late 1950s who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy. Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that the massive life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

Industry News: Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Include Disney World

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • In a recent development, walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida.
  • It has been revealed that rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson stated the decision to came down to resources and story reasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, walt Disney World is synonymous with Florida, but the iconic theme park doesn't show up in Rockstar's GTA 6, which takes place in a fictional Florida called Leonida. Many are wondering why, especially when GTA: Vice City had its own parody of the theme park--Fun World--many years ago. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson mentioned the decision to came down to resources and story reasons. “A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there,” he told VGC. Nelson added that Rockstar isn't known to cut corners, so if GTA 6 were to have its own version of Walt Disney World, it would be a "fully functioning theme park," and that just wasn't doable. Walt Disney World is much more than just its most famous park, Magic Kingdom. The property includes three other main parks, Animal Kingdom, Hollywood Studios, and Epcot, along with the Disney Springs shopping district, multiple water parks and golf courses, and more than two-dozen hotels. The entire property is more than 25,000 acres. Even if Rockstar were to replicate only a portion of the scale of the real Walt Disney World, it would surely be a big job. Players might expect fully functioning rides, and Nelson said the challenge for Rockstar would be, "Where do you stop? When do you feel like it's enough?" Nelson said people think Rockstar has unlimited time and money, and that isn't true. "So sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to,” he said. Plus, as Nelson pointed out, there would need to be a story reason to send Jason and Lucia hundreds of miles north from Miami to Orlando, where Walt Disney World is. GTA 6 has a huge map, but it's contained to Vice City and its surrounding areas--it doesn't go that far north.

It has been revealed that use of generative AI in game dev remains as contentious as it does ubiquitous—a recent GDC report found that around 40% of devs use AI, but more than half think its influence has been negative. Ubisoft is continuing to double down on the technology, this time with Motherbrain, a upcoming subsidiary fashioned from the team behind its "first playable generative AI experience.".

As reported by VGC, Motherbrain's purpose is to develop "AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences … Its current focus is on new player experiences, smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large scale systemic worlds," according to an earnings report which was released Thursday.

The information comes at a turbulent time for the publishing giant, which just laid off 166 employees even after Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced "outperformed expectations." A sweeping internal overhaul earlier this year saw the manufacturer reorganize its workforce into a throng of "creative houses," a decision which led to swathes of layoffs and six project cancellations, including the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake.

According to recent reports, it's not clear what Motherbrain are at work on, in specific terms, right now, but there may be some clues in its past work. That playable AI "experience" I mentioned earlier is none other than Teammates, an R&D project based on a prior experiment with uncanny AI "neo-NPCs.".

Recent findings suggest that teammates aimed to allow players to command NPC squadmates in a rudimentary shooter game with a microphone, and using AI, have those squadmates react believably. It's not far off, at least conceptually, from what we've seen in games like Where Winds Meet and Fortnite, both of which have experimented with AI-powered NPCs.

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games.

Tens of millions of people are playing Grand Theft Auto 6 right now. What’s the best way to experience Rockstar’s latest open-world epic? According to one of the developers themselves, you should play it with as little anxiety around checklists and online noise as possible.

It has been revealed that âThere is so much to do in Leonida, and so much to discover, that we hope players get to the point where they stop thinking in tasks, completion percentages, online guides and rather let the game unfold in front of them,” VP of design Stephen Donkin said in a packet of studio development notes shared with press. “When you play the game and take your time with it, playing at the pace it asks you to, it can really unfold in front of you in a way that can feel almost infinite at a macro level, but each individual encounter still feels hand-crafted and with a human behind it.

Donkin’s first Rockstar credit was as a QA tester on GTA 5, and his advice for GTA 6 players echoed the feelings of some of the studio’s other developers when it comes to taking in the immersive beauty and emergent nuance of the new entry’s complex world. âThere are clearly tons of high-stakes, high-energy, fast-paced moments and thrills and laughs along the way, but there are also quiet, meditative experiences and adventures to be had that offer a fully different feeling,” remarked senior design director Ghyan Koehne. “If I had to be held to a single feeling, Iâd say âwonder.â We want players to be constantly presented with a feeling of wonderâwe hope everyone feels a mixture of emotions.â.

According to recent reports, it’s a stark contrast to how GTA lives in the popular imagination of most people, which is as a chaos sim full of drugs, sex, and violent crime. GTA 6 has those things, but they are far less domineering parts of the experience this time around. It’s also completely divorced from how some people often experience modern video games, which is heavily augmented by a second-screen experience full of achievement guides, TikTok memes, and social media rage-bait.

Recent findings suggest that people should play GTA 6 however they want, but I’d encourage them to take at least a few hours to experience the game in the dark with headphones on and as little knowledge as possible of what awaits them and how the whole thing works, their phones and laptops safely tucked away in a different room. Former Kotaku editor Kirk Hamilton was famous for telling people to turn off parts of the onscreen UI to make the experience more immersive and make it feel less like a chore list. Every massive upcoming open-world game that came out there would be a post about turning off the minimap.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve never been able to play games that way. I’m too fidgety and squirrely for that kind of thing. But I always try to spend at least a couple hours in that headspace, treating what’s in front of me more as something worth experiencing for its own sake than just as a maze to speedrun through as efficiently as possible in exchange for in-game rewards, entertaining setpieces, and satisfying emotional climaxes. That’s an increasingly alien way of approaching anything in our algorithmically optimized world, but GTA 6 offers as good a reason as any to try it.

“If players can let go and submit to becoming immersed in the world of Leonida, and just follow their nose as they play, they will feel the Leonida I have felt,” Donkin mentioned, “And thatâs all we could ask for.â.

  • Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the upcoming movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when Francis Lawrence, the filmmaker behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, greets me over Zoom, he’s aware that his darkly lit, gothic backdrop makes him look a bit like the villainous President Snow. “All I need is a significant eagle back here,” the white-haired, smartly dressed director jokes.

Lawrence has helmed almost every film in Lionsgate’s blockbuster series, based on Suzanne Collins’s best-selling novels about a dystopia where a bloodthirsty dictator forces children to fight to the death for the elite’s entertainment. He joined the franchise for its 2013 sequel, Catching Fire, and has directed only three non–Hunger Games movies in the decade-plus since. In that time, one could argue, the world has tilted further toward the oppressive future depicted in Collins’s novels—see, for instance, Donald Trump’s Hunger Games–esque Patriot Games. And while Lawrence isn’t naming names, he’s never lost sight of the movies’ larger political message. “I feel really lucky to be able to tell stories that matter, that are wrapped in these commercial packages,” he tells Vanity Fair. “So anytime one of these things comes around, I jump at it.”.

Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the upcoming movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada. He plays the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch Abernathy, a victor of the Hunger Games who later serves as a mentor to actor Lawrence’s Katniss Everdeen. Making a reflective movie prompted director Lawrence to reflect on his own Hollywood trajectory. “The biggest difference is that I’m a lot more relaxed. I was nervous as hell on Catching Fire,” he claims. “It was my fourth movie. It was a movie I was inheriting. It was a massive movie, and it was a massive cast. So I was really intimidated. Now I have much more fun, I will say. I’m much more comfortable with actors, and the amount of actors, and with logistics. And there’s definitely a family that’s built into it, which is very key for me. There’s, what, 14 years of my life spent making these movies? So it has to be fun.”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: When did you become aware of Sunrise on the Reaping, and at what point did you and Suzanne Collins start discussing an adaptation?

In a recent development, francis Lawrence: When we did the original series of movies, and we finished the last Mockingjay, she remarked she was done, and we thought that was it. Then she surprised me and Nina [Jacobson], the producer, with Ballad, however many years later. And she never tells us when she’s writing. Even when she has something to read, she never tells us what it’s about. She’s very superstitious about it all. So we got the call, which was very exciting. And she said, “Go to my agent’s house. There’s a manuscript. Let’s talk after you read it.”.

I got to his house, sat in his backyard, and there was a manuscript and a copy of Catching Fire sitting on top of it with a few tabs in it. I opened to the tabs and saw that it had the portion where Katniss and Peeta were looking up the Haymitch Games, that sequence from the book. And I was like, Oh, she’s written the Haymitch story, which was very exciting. And that started the process that we always have, which is that I read the manuscript in one sitting, then read it a second time after having a conversation with Suzanne.

According to recent reports, then I fly to Latest York and meet her at Scholastic, and we sit up in a conference room for about a week going through the book, beat by beat, of what we think the movie is going to be. She and I lay it all out and chat, and she sits on her computer and writes a scriptment. Then that’s the thing that we turn over to the screenwriter.

How have you built that trust with the author of these books, having adapted them for more than a decade now?

Industry observers note that that working process happened accidentally when I signed on to do Catching Fire. I had never done a sequel to someone else’s first movie before. And when Lionsgate and the first director, [Gary Ross], parted ways and I got the call, they didn’t have a script, but they had started the process of developing it before I was on board. And so I signed on based on the book and had planned a trip to Fresh York to meet with Suzanne.

According to recent reports, the script came on the day that I was traveling to Upcoming York. I read it, and it was not the movie that I wanted to make—because I loved the book, and it was not the book. Luckily, nobody else wanted to make that version of the movie either. Our meeting of me just picking her brain turned into, “This script doesn’t work. Let’s go through, page by page, and figure out the version of the movie we want to make.”.

In a recent development, that’s what really formed the bond—just working really, really closely with her. Spending 8 or 10 hours a day for a week or two in a conference room—me riffing on visual ideas and her talking about the story. We think the same way in terms of storytelling, structure, and she seemed to take to my visual ideas.

Sources indicate that there’s this weird dynamic that happens as we get closer to production. We’re usually developing the script pretty much within a week of shooting. But the production is also building. So you have thousands of people working, figuring out locations, traveling in different parts of the world. The stress levels are building.

Suzanne and I have related the relationship to almost like a mother-son relationship. It starts really lovely and creative, but then as we get closer and closer, it’s me being that late teen who’s ready to leave the home, like, Okay, enough’s enough. I’m going to go make the movie now. I have to say, I love the process. It’s not without its stress sometimes, but that’s part of the closeness of it all that I cherish.

How did this film’s futuristic-meets-1970s aesthetic come about?

According to recent reports, there was an element [of the story] that reminded me a bit of Alice in Wonderland, which then made me think of Jefferson Airplane, that song “White Rabbit,” which brought me to the ’60s and ’70s. Then you can look at characters certain ways. Like, Haymitch, you go, Okay, he’s from, like, young Bruce Springsteen, or Lenore Dove [played by Whitney Peak], like a young Stevie Nicks. And you get this hippie vibe. And the Capitol is that Warhol Studio 54 crowd, and Snow like a ’70s Yves Saint Laurent.

How do you go about casting a young Haymitch, finding an actor who can anchor the film like Jennifer Lawrence did in the original Hunger Games film?

Sources indicate that our casting director, Deb Zane, had met him, and I want to say before he did East of Eden. She had a lot of faith in him. We liked his self-tape a lot. But we knew that he was going to have to pull a lot off. He starts as a very optimistic, fun, playful, young guy in love, and in this movie has to turn into somebody that’s much closer to the Haymitch that we’re used to—cynical and a drunk. He’s going to have to go through a lot of emotional trauma, plus have that kind of mischievousness, irreverence, all these different elements that Woody [Harrelson] has naturally. And so we really put him through the ringer. We did a lot of tests, kept bringing him back, bringing him back, bringing him back. He and I were modulating how much Woody we feel in his performance.

I want to make sure that everybody makes the role their own. That they find the spirit of the character and that it’s not trying to do an imitation of somebody. That’s true of Elle [Fanning] doing Effie, of Ralph [Fiennes] doing Snow, of Jesse [Plemons] doing Plutarch, Kieran [Culkin] as Caesar. Everybody has to figure out how to do it on their own. Then the weird thing is that Kelvin [Harrison Jr., who plays a young Beetee], has worked with Jeffrey [Wright] three times. So he’s fairly close with Jeffrey. When he got the role, he called and said, “You won’t believe this, but I’m actually playing the young version of you.” He could just conjure Jeffrey Wright. His voice, the speech patterns, the timbre of the sound of everything. It was pretty wild.

Were there storylines from the previous films that you felt you could plant Easter eggs for? I’m thinking specifically of the romantic chemistry between Effie and Haymitch.

There are certain Capitol characters where I give a lot of freedom for improvisation. Effie, Caesar, Drusilla [played by Glenn Close], there’s a lot of room for ad-libs. One of the elements that we definitely played with a bit came from an improvised moment in the [last] Mockingjay. We were shooting this scene in Atlanta outside of Snow’s mansion, which is one of the very last scenes of Katniss in the Capitol. She’s saying goodbye to Effie, and then Haymitch and Effie kiss.

Quite honestly, it was an idea because Woody just wanted to kiss Elizabeth Banks. But everybody thought it would be fun and that the fans would dig it, that Haymitch kissed her. Then it became this substantial thing of this hidden love that Haymitch and Effie have for one another. And Elle played into that a bit. So there’s, I would say, a hint of flirtation here between the two, less so on Haymitch’s side. His heart is obviously somewhere else in the story. But Elle definitely brought a bit of that to it. That was not scripted. That’s the fun of having great actors.

What was it like to reunite Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson from the original movies?

In a recent development, jen and I have stayed close over the years. We’ve done four movies together. Josh, who basically has moved to Spain, I haven’t seen in a long time. Woody I see off and on and text every once in a while. But there was something really special about the three of them being back together.

According to recent reports, it’s also really, for the most part, the same crew from 2012, when we started making Catching Fire. It’s the same DP [Jo Willems], the same camera operator [David J. Thompson], the same AD [Christopher Surgent].

[When] they got to the hotel, Jen and Josh were in the bar having a beer or something, and I was like, Okay, I won’t even shower. I won’t get out of my rain gear. I’ll just come in. The next thing you know, there were 40 of us who had been together since Catching Fire, the gang back together. It’s like a high school reunion or something, but in the best possible way.

There’s a futility to what happens in this film, knowing where we end up in future movies. How do you handle that aspect of history being doomed to repeat itself?

Look, we’re doing a story where you know the lead character is going to make it out. It’s really about how he makes it out, and what he ends up being like at the end of it all. What I’m really pleased about is that the way Suzanne wrote the book, and the way I think we’ve ended the movie, there is a sense of hope that the tragedy is not for nothing. That was really notable to me. And one of the beautiful elements in the story, which comes a bit later, is this sense of, everybody has to find their voice. Everybody has to participate.

It really deals with this thing that I think is happening a lot today, where you find apathy: people not wanting to vote, feeling even if they do vote that it’s not going to matter. This idea that you have to be active, and you can’t expect immediate gratification—that everybody needs to stand up and it may take generations, but you still have to do it.

Outside of my screening on the Upper West Side, there was a group protesting Elon Musk and data centers because the documentary about him was playing at the theater. It was a reminder that there will always be something to rise up against, and always people who will be willing to do it.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, exactly. And ideally, at some point, if everybody stands up, something will change.

Sources indicate that during the 13 years that you’ve worked in this universe, dystopia has felt more and more familiar. How have real-world events influenced your filmmaking?

Sources indicate that in the 56 years I’ve been alive, there’s never really been a time where I’ve felt like, Oh wow, everything is great. Nothing is wrong in the world. It always feels like there’s some dystopian sense about the world at any given time. And somehow Suzanne is always able to write these stories about it, which is what makes these movies feel timeless. A lot of people just see them as spectacles, but really they’re about our times very specifically. Almost in a subversive way, I feel like we’ve gotten to smuggle these ideas into these movies that a lot of people go see.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • Recent findings suggest that that's now changing.
  • In a recent development, as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

Recent findings suggest that that's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an important account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a newly introduced "View Once" option as well.

In a recent development, as WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

According to recent reports, as mentioned above, this feature is at the moment in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That said, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

In a recent development, if you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest update. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

According to recent reports, bassam Tariq directed 2026’s critically-lauded action-thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother starring Mahershala Ali. He was also supposed to direct Ali in Marvel’s period-piece Blade reboot, but getting that project off the ground ended up being a nightmare for everyone involved. Tariq said he’ll never put himself in that situation again.

“It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script. You’re sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you,” he noted in a fresh interview with New Arab (via IGN). “That’s also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn’t add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I’ve been thinking about that a lot.”.

Recent findings suggest that to recap how the whole Blade mess went, Marvel first announced a latest movie for its Black vampire hunter in 2019 with Ali as the star. Tariq, whose only credit at the time was 2020’s Mogul Mowgli, wasn’t signed on to direct until 2021. But there was still no script, and apparently nothing nailed down about what the final movie would look like. Tariq left the project just a year later and was replaced by Yann Demange (â71 and Lovecraft Country). He would end up leaving the project as well just two years later. Swirling around the troubled production were changing mandates from the top of Disney and rumors that Blade’s role in the Blade movie was shrinking.

It has been revealed that “If you’re the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you’re not the one making any of these decisionsâand it’s actually coming from a corporate entityâthat’s not a great way to be a director,” Tariq told Newly introduced Arab. “I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn’t a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life’s too short to make sh*t films, so that was my major lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it’s between them and me. It’s quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.”.

Marvel Studios director Kevin Feige has since blamed himself for the breakdown, saying this past summer that he felt, âlike a gigantic loser and failure that we didnât get off the ground with Mahershala.â Ali has also moved on from the mess. “For whatever reason, that project is not for me,â he noted in July. âIf they wanted to do it, we wouldâve done it. So I have to move on, and I have moved on.â.

He continued, “In that way, I feel creatively redeemed on some level, just in my own journey between me, myself, and I. But I feel ready to move on from theÂ Blade questions. Those questions are for them. They didnât want to do it, so they should answer that question.” There was one silver-lining to the whole debacle, which is that the costumes designed for the Blade movie ended up getting used in Sinners.

Skydance producers are reassuring the team that all is well, despite rumors to the contrary.

Even artwork will be generated with AI.

Regular viewers only got access to three of the four newly introduced scenes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the upcoming one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The company has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings. If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms. Current free game at Epic This week's free game is Mark of the Deep, a 2025 pirate-themed adventure with a mix of Metroidvania and soulslike gameplay. Next free games at Epic Next week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. See all free games at Epic Epic Games Store free games list We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic users have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the new one(s) take their place. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Candace Cameron Bure is counting down the days until she can enjoy her newly expanded family’s merry holiday season with her two infant grandchildren in her arms.

“I know everyone’s grandchild is the cutest baby in the whole world, and mine are the cutest in the whole world because they’re mine,” Cameron Bure, 50, told People in an interview published Saturday, November 21, also revealing her “whole family” will be together on Thanksgiving and Christmas this year.

“Some family is flying in,” the Full House alum teased. “It’s going to be a massive family Thanksgiving and Christmas, and I couldn’t be more thrilled.”.

Recent findings suggest that candace and her husband, Valeri Bure, are parents of daughter Natasha, 28, and sons Lev, 26, and Maksim, 24. The married couple recently became grandparents in September when Lev’s wife, Elliott Bure, gave birth to son Bond 10 weeks early. Natasha revealed the next month that she welcomed her first baby, daughter Winnie, with husband Bradley Steven Perry.

After Bond and Winnie’s arrivals, Candace has fully embraced her grandmother era — or “CandyGram” as she prefers to be called.

“It’s been incredible. There’s nothing like watching your own child become a parent,” Candace exclusively told Us earlier this month. “We just love the time and soaking it all up, and it’s been amazing.”.

According to Valeri, 52, he can barely find time to pry his wife away from the babies.

Industry observers note that “Candace is a baby hogger. She is the worst,” he jokingly told Us. “I would hold my grandkid and she would run up and just start taking it away and I’m like, ‘Stop, stop!’ I’m like, ‘This is my turn to hold the baby.’ So, I learned that she is a baby hogger. She’s taking it away from me.”.

Candace, who openly admitted to hogging Bond and Winnie’s snuggles, is also in awe that their arrivals made the former hockey star a “softy” in their presence.

“Listen, this is my time,” he quipped. “[Our kids are] like, ‘This is not our papa that we grew up with. Who is this person?’ I’m like, ‘Why is your baby crying? Give it to me. Like, baby should not be crying.’ Our kids was like, ‘Nope, they gotta cry it out.’ No crying for the grandbabies.”.

Candace and Valeri, who have been married for 30 years, have also been doling out helpful parenting advice to their kids.

“You know, for me, and I like to be involved into the family, like don’t miss the little things, and even you don’t realize how much effect you have on a kid just doing something small,” he told Us. “Because when we talk with our kids, and we’re like, ‘What’s a memory that you take away?’ And all of a sudden they throw the story at you that you don’t even remember it.”.

Recent findings suggest that he continued, “I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, you remember this story?’ So, you know, the kids are watching you, and just to be there for every moment because you know when you get older the time kind of speeds up. … My best advice is just soak it up, enjoy this moment.”.

#51457. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1007 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • Sources indicate that proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

According to recent reports, you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

Sources indicate that proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—currently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

As the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

Recent findings suggest that for the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Industry observers note that pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

What's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

Now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

To be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

Recent findings suggest that however, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

Image and video detection is the newly introduced string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

Again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

Next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

In a recent development, here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

Sources indicate that I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran showed that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a post to X, "The Everything App," US entertainment and communications conglomerate Comcast revealed that Grand Theft Auto 6's historic launch drove record-breaking internet traffic. According to Comcast, only a quarter of "the entire internet" was downloading Rockstar's latest cozy game phenomenon.

Sources indicate that "GTA 6 didn't just break records in gaming," Comcast wrote. "Its launch drove the biggest internet traffic day in our network history, with traffic climbing 31% above an average day. At peak, GTA 6 accounted for nearly a quarter of all network traffic.".

Recent findings suggest that comcast shared a video of a line graph showing the massive relative spike in activity on November 19. The chart is unlabeled except for the date, but it presumably corresponds to the volume of data being downloaded across Comcast's entire network.

And that last but does add a caveat to the numbers Comcast cited: Its network and "the entire internet" are two different things, unless I'm missing something here or Comcast's data accounts for other ISPs and other countries, not just its own services.

Regardless, it's still a significant bit of fun with statistics, another example of the totalizing footprint of what may be the largest commercial launch in entertainment history. Imagine how much bigger it would have been launching on PC as well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's Grand Theft Auto VI day around the world--the game is really good, as it turns out. While players are out exploring the massive in-game map or checking their in-game phones as much as they check their real-life ones, Rockstar has celebrated the occasion by releasing the full cast list for its new crime epic. Nestled among celebrity names like Bad Bunny, "Weird Al" Yankovic, Brigitte Nielsen, Stephen Root, and Bobby Moynihan is a name that will surprise many longtime Rockstar fans. It's also, potentially, a GTA VI spoiler, so we're going to put it below a selfie of co-protagonist Jason Duval. Seriously, if you want to go into Grand Theft Auto VI spoiler-free, look away now. Do you think Jason's last name is a Jacksonville Jaguars reference? DUUUUUVAL! Alright, if you're still here, then you're in for the spoiler. Ready? Here goes: One of the names listed on the credits is Michael Hollick, playing a role known only as "The Hitman." If that's setting off a signal to established Grand Theft Auto fans, it's because Michael Hollick is also the voice of GTA IV protagonist--and occasional hitman--Niko Bellic. Hollick's involvement in GTA VI is surprising, considering how just after GTA IV's release in 2008, he publicly criticized Rockstar for his payment on the project. As reported by CNET by way of the New York Times, Hollick reportedly was paid $100,000 for 15 months of work on the project. Whether or not this is actually a spoiler remains to be seen, but with Grand Theft Auto VI now available on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, we imagine the truth will be revealed soon enough.
